rationale:
Following workflow-based recommendation because:

1. HIGH coordination complexity (42.9% coordination functions)
   - Checkout orchestration requires coordinating 4+ services
   - Complex state management across inventory, payment, order
   - Compensation logic on failure (distributed rollback)

2. CROSS_DOMAIN workflow span (100% cross-domain flows)
   - All workflows touch multiple domains (cart, inventory, payment, order)
   - Standard Checkout Flow spans 8 steps across domains
   - Failure handling requires cross-domain compensation

3. Workflow-heavy operations (not simple CRUD)
   - Multi-step orchestration with business logic
   - State tracking and error handling
   - Distributed transaction management

Workflow-based organization keeps coordination LOCAL within CheckoutWorkflowService instead of distributed across domain services. This:
- Reduces distributed state complexity
- Simplifies error handling and compensation logic
- Makes workflows easier to understand and maintain
- Improves testability (mock interfaces instead of multiple services)

Anti-pattern avoided: Domain-based (UserService, ProductService, OrderService) would scatter checkout logic and create distributed state management problems.

workflow_services.responsibility: Orchestrate entire checkout process (initiate, validate, coordinate inventory/payment/order)
workflow_services.coordination_logic: All checkout coordination stays LOCAL in this service

domain_capability_services.responsibility: Provide order management and notification capabilities
